deep.reconstruction:
Notation (mine): φ(q)=Σ_{n∈Z} q^{n²}=1+2q+2q⁴+2q⁹+…, ψ(q)=Σ_{n≥0} q^{n(n+1)/2}=1+q+q³+q⁶+…, (q;q)_∞=Π(1-q^n), and χ(n)=(n/3), the Legendre symbol mod 3 (1, -1, 0 for n≡1, 2, 0 mod 3). Ramanujan writes x for q. The page is page (2) of a list of numbered Lambert-series identities for theta quotients. The series of headings 1.1x, 1.2x, …, 1.7x tracks the level (1, 3, 5, 6, 7) and continues on the next page. No derivations are written; only the statements appear.

(1.13) φ(q)⁶ = 1 − 4 Σ_{n≥1} χ₄(n) n² qⁿ/(1−qⁿ) + 16 Σ_{n≥1} n² qⁿ/(1+q^{2n}). Here χ₄ is the nonprincipal character mod 4; the first sum is 1²q/(1−q) − 3²q³/(1−q³) + 5²q⁵/(1−q⁵) − …. Taking coefficients gives Jacobi's six-square theorem: r₆(N) = 16 Σ_{d|N} χ₄(N/d) d² − 4 Σ_{d|N} χ₄(d) d².

(1.14) φ(q)⁸ = 1 + 16 Σ_{n≥1} n³ qⁿ/(1−(−q)ⁿ). The terms read 1³q/(1+q) + 2³q²/(1−q²) + 3³q³/(1+q³) + …. This is equivalent to Jacobi's eight-square theorem: r₈(N) = 16 Σ_{d|N} (−1)^{N+d} d³.

(1.21) Written with double signs: (1∓2q+2q⁴∓2q⁹…)³/(1∓2q³+2q¹²∓…) = 1 ∓ 6(q/(1+q) − q²/(1+q²) + q⁴/(1+q⁴) − q⁵/(1+q⁵) + …).
- Upper (minus) sign: φ(−q)³/φ(−q³) = 1 − 6 Σ χ(n) qⁿ/(1+qⁿ). This is correct.
- Lower (plus) sign, read literally with the same right-hand bracket: it fails (see errors).
- The correct companion, obtained by q→−q (my derivation): φ(q)³/φ(q³) = 1 + 6(q/(1−q) + q²/(1+q²) − q⁴/(1+q⁴) − q⁵/(1−q⁵) + …).

(1.22) φ(q³)³/φ(q) = 1 − 2 Σ χ(n) qⁿ/(1−(−q)ⁿ). The terms read q/(1+q) − q²/(1−q²) + q⁴/(1−q⁴) − q⁵/(1+q⁵) + ….

(1.31) ψ(q)³/ψ(q³) = 1 + 3 Σ_{n≥0} [q^{6n+1}/(1−q^{6n+1}) − q^{6n+5}/(1−q^{6n+5})].

(1.32) q ψ(q³)³/ψ(q) = Σ_{n≥1} χ(n) qⁿ/(1−q^{2n}).

(1.41) This identity is completed on the next page. (q;q)³_∞/(q³;q³)_∞ = 1 − 3 Σ χ(n) qⁿ/(1−qⁿ) + 9 Σ χ(n) q^{3n}/(1−q^{3n}). In Borwein notation this is b(q) = (3a(q³) − a(q))/2, where a(q) = 1 + 6 Σ χ(n) qⁿ/(1−qⁿ).

Verification by hand (mine):
- (1.13), (1.14): r₆(1)=12, r₆(2)=60 and r₈(1)=16 are reproduced.
- (1.21), upper sign: both sides are 1−6q+12q²−6q³−6q⁴+….
- (1.22): both sides are 1−2q+4q²−2q³+2q⁴+….
- (1.31): both sides are 1+3q+3q²+3q³+3q⁴+0q⁵+….
- (1.32): both sides are q−q²+q³+q⁴+0q⁵+….
- (1.41): both sides are 1−3q+0q²+….
errors: (1.21): if the double sign is read so that the lower choice gives φ(q)³/φ(q³) = 1 + 6(q/(1+q) − q²/(1+q²) + q⁴/(1+q⁴) − …), that version is false. The q² coefficient is +12 on the left and −12 on the right.
In (1.21) only the minus-sign case φ(−q)³/φ(−q³) is valid as written. A correct plus-sign version needs the bracket transformed by q→−q, i.e. q/(1−q) + q²/(1+q²) − q⁴/(1+q⁴) − q⁵/(1−q⁵) + ….
Either Ramanujan's corrected ∓/± signs are ambiguous in the image, or the double sign is a slip. All other identities on the page check correctly to several terms.

results.modern_name: Level-3 (cubic) theta quotient Lambert series identities
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (notebooks; cf. Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks III); cubic theory by J.M. & P.B. Borwein (1991)

results.what: (1.31), (1.32) ψ(q)^3/ψ(q^3) and qψ(q^3)^3/ψ(q) as Lambert series

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard theta/Lambert-series identities. Two are Jacobi's classical theorems on sums of squares, and the level-3 identities are known entries of Ramanujan's notebooks treated by Berndt. The page is a clean list of known results; the only notable feature is a sign issue in (1.21).
